texts.preamble: Inderjeet Kaur vs Anil Kumar Singhal on 7 March, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Divya Malhotra : Senior Civil Judge Cum Rent Controller : North District : Rohini Courts : Delhi. Inderjeet Kaur Wife of Late Harjeet Singh Khurana R/o D - 14A/29, Ground Floor, Model Town - Ii, Delhi - 110009. Also at : F-14/60-61, Model Town - Ii, Delhi - 110009. .....Petitioner Versus Anil Kumar Singhal Son of Late Chajju Ram Prop. M/s Vinod Departmental Store F - 14/61, Model Town - Ii, Delhi - 110009. .....Respondent Cnr No. Dlnt 0300 1120 2023 Rc Arc No. 23/2023 Petition for eviction under Section Under Section 14 (1)(e) r/w Section 25B of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958. Date of Filing 27.05.2023 Date of Reserving of Order 13.02.2025 Date of Final Order 07.03.2025
texts.facts: ORDER By way of this order, the application for leave to defend filed by the tenant in an eviction petition under Section 14(1)(e) r/w Section 25B of the Delhi Rent Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as the "DRCA" or the "Act") is being decided. PETITION Inderjeet Kaur vs Anil Kumar Singhal on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120685659/ 1 1. Gurbax Singh and his wife Harbhajan Kaur were owners of several properties including property bearing no. F-14/60-61, Model Town II, Delhi (in short the "property in question"). During their lifetime, they had let out a portion of this property i.e. a shop at F-14/61, admeasuring 30'' X 9'', Model Town II, Delhi - 09 (in short the "tenanted premises"), more specifically shown in red color in the site plan, to one Chajju Mal. After they passed away, disputes arose between their sons Harjeet Singh Khurana (petitioner's husband) and Mohan Bir Singh which they both attempted to resolve through arbitration. Unconvinced by the award of the arbitrator, Harjeet Singh approached the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in OMP No. 517/2009 titled "Harjit Singh Vs. Mohan Bir Singh". The brothers eventually resolved their disputes and arrived at a settlement which was recorded vide order dated 05.04.2019 (in short the "settlement order") by the Hon'ble High Court. By virtue of such settlement, the left side portion of the property in question admeasuring 444 sq. yards came into the share of petitioner's husband Harjeet Singh while Mohan Bir Singh took the right side portion measuring 400 sq. yards of the same RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 2 of 25 property. Both the brothers duly acted upon the settlement and took possession of their respective shares. The tenanted premises is stated to have fallen in Harjeet Singh's share and during his lifetime he had also renovated the front portion of the property F-14/60-61 and had let out the same on rent to M/s Kwality Bazar. 2. Harjeet Singh passed away on 12.10.2022 leaving behind the petitioner and their three children as his legal heirs. After the death of her husband, petitioner wishes to start her own business for which purpose she requires the tenanted premises. As the original tenant Chajju Mal has already expired, she has filed the present eviction petition against his son i.e. respondent who apparently is running a kirana shop from the premises. Petitioner is not aware of the monthly rent as the property was let out by her predecessors and the rent used to be collected by her brother-in-law Mohan Bir previously. 3. Petitioner states that she wants to open a beauty parlor in order to keep herself busy and to have an independent source of income. She will start her business with the help of her daughter-in- laws and sister and the location of tenanted premises is ideal for the said purpose as it is in close proximity of Model Town Residential Area. Further, the respondent himself has successfully obtained eviction orders against his tenants in two eviction petitions bearing RC No. 17/19 titled "Anil Kumar Singhal Vs. Jaswant Singh" and RC No. 31/18 titled "Anil Kumar Singhal Vs. Gian Singh" which were allowed by the then Ld. ARC, North on 26.10.2021. These eviction RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 3 of 25 petitions were filed by the respondent as landlord/owner, wherein he had inter alia stated that he wished to shift his departmental store namely M/s Vinod Departmental Store from F-14/61 (i.e. the present tenanted premises) to F-14/64 as both the properties were hardly 100 feet away; as the customers were locally based; as the property under his occupation was a tenanted property wherein he was apprehending eviction and as the shifting would not cause loss of business to him. 4. Thus, as the respondent himself has obtained possession of two properties under his ownership on the basis of his bonafide requirement and as the tenanted premises is the most ideal property for her requirements, the present eviction petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section Inderjeet Kaur vs Anil Kumar Singhal on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120685659/ 2 14(1)(e) r/w Section 25B DRCA. In support of her petition, she has relied upon a site plan, photographs of the tenanted premises; copy of order dated 05.04.2019 of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in OMP 517/2009; copy of Death Certificate of her husband and copies of eviction orders dated 26.10.2021 in RC No. 17/19 and RC No. 31/18. LEAVE TO DEFEND APPLICATION 5. The respondent has resisted the eviction petition on several grounds. They can be broadly categorized as under :- A. Landlord - Tenant Relationship - It is stated that there is no landlord-tenant relationship between the parties; that the landlord of the respondent is Mohan Bir Singh (petitioner's brother-in-law) RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 4 of 25 which is evidenced from the three rent receipts pertaining to 1980's/1990's as well as copy of challans of deposition of rent for the year 2002, filed by the respondent on record; that Mohan Bir used to withdraw rent from the Court; that the petitioner never demanded/received rent from the respondent; that in 2001 Mohan Bir Singh had also filed an eviction petition under Section 14(1)(a), DRCA against the respondent's mother titled "Mohan Bir Singh Vs. Satyawati & Ors." , which got abated on account of her death; that Mohan Bir Singh has not been made a party to the proceedings; that no title document has been filed by the petitioner; that the lease deed of adjacent tenant namely Kwality Bazar has also not been filed and the landlord of Kwality Bazar is one M/s United Sales Agency/HUF and not petitioner's husband as claimed by her; that the petition is bad for non-joinder of other LRs of Harjeet Singh Khurana and that attornment notice has ever been issued by petitioner. B. Bonafide Requirement - It is stated that the requirement of the petitioner is not bonafide; that the property bearing no. F-14/60- 61 is a huge one admeasuring 910 square yards (excluding the tenanted shop); that there are already two shops on the ground floor of property bearing no. F-14/60-61, which are lying vacant along with halls on the upper floors which can be utilized by the petitioner for her purported need; that a board with "Space Available for Rent" is hanging on these vacant shops; that petitioner has concealed the true position of the property by not filing the complete site plan; that the area under occupation of the respondent is merely 200 square feet (8' RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 5 of 25 x 25') as evidenced from the site plan of earlier eviction proceedings and wrongly mentioned in the present petition to be 270 square feet; that a beauty parlor cannot be run from such a small space in which a kirana shop is being run; that petitioner has no experience to run a beauty parlor and that she has not even stated her need to be bonafide. Inderjeet Kaur vs Anil Kumar Singhal on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120685659/ 3 C. Alternative Suitable Accommodation - It is stated that Harjeet Singh Khurana during his life time owned a commercial plot bearing no. 2638, Hamilton Road, Kashmiri Gate, Delhi, where around 400 square feet portion is lying vacant; that petitioner owns a huge multi-storeyed property named "Paradise" at D-14A/29, Model Town II, Delhi admeasuring 1100 square yards, which has not been disclosed by her and can be used to set up a beauty parlor; that petitioner failed to aver that she does not have any other suitable accommodation and that in view of availability of two shops at the ground floor of the property in question, present is the case of additional accommodation. D. Other Grounds - Apart from above, it is stated that petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e. the remaining LRs/children of Late Harjeet Singh Khurana as well as Mohan Bir Singh; that the petitioner has not waited for the statutory period of five years as provided u/s 14 (6) of DRCA; that the petitioner has not filed the complete site plan and has not come to the court with clean hands for having concealed the availability of two vacant shops in the same property and that it also needs to be investigated who is the landlord RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 6 of 25 of M/s Kwality Bazar as it appears to be one HUF M/s United Sales Agency. On these grounds leave to defend the case, has been sought. 6. In support of his application, respondent has relied upon old rent receipts and challans (supra); copy of eviction petition filed by Mohan Bir against the respondent and his family members in 2001; site plan; copy of rent receipt issued by United State Agency to Kwality Bazar alongwith its GST details; some photographs of property in question as well as of petitioner's property namely Paradise; photographs of respondent's shop etc.
texts.arguments: Reliance in this regard can be placed upon "Dhannalal v. Kalawatibai & Ors.", (2002) 6 SCC 16, wherein it was held that even one co-owner/landlord can file a suit for ejectment against the tenant and it is not necessary that all co-owners/landlords must jointly sue for ejectment. This principle is based on the doctrine of agency and one co-owner filing a suit for eviction against the tenant does so on his behalf in his own right as well as an agent of the other co-owners. Neither the court nor RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 14 of 25 the tenant can dictate to the landlord which floor or which space she should use for her business (see "Uday Shankar Upadhyay & Ors. Vs. Naveen Maheshwari, (2010) 1 SCC 503"). 19. In "Shiv Sarup Gupta Vs Dr. Mahesh Chand Gupta" AIR 1999 SC 2507, Hon'ble Supreme Court held that:- "Needless to say that an alternate accommodation, to entail denial of the claim of the landlord, must be reasonably suitable, obviously in comparison with RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 16 of 25 the suit accommodation wherefrom the landlord is seeking eviction. Convenience and safety of the landlord and his family members would be relevant fact. While considering the totality of the circumstances, the court may keep in view the profession or vocation of the landlord and his family members, their style of living, their habits and the background wherefrom they come." 23. Respondent has argued that the need of the petitioner is not genuine. He states that petitioner is around 64 years of age, inexperienced and it would be preposterous to expect that she could venture into a new business at such an advanced age that too from a small shop admeasuring 200 sq feet which is currently being used as a grocery/departmental store by the respondent. 25. Petitioner is a widowed lady who wants to run her own business and stand on her own feet. Merely because she is 64 years of age would not debar her from venturing into new avenues in life. Any person can have a fresh start at any stage and age in life and the legislature has not put a number on the same. It is petitioner's fundamental right to enter into a vocation or business of her choice irrespective of her age and respondent is no one to say otherwise. Her lack of previous experience would also not come in her way and same is quite immaterial while deciding her bonafides. Reference in the said context may be had to the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Inderjeet Kaur vs Anil Kumar Singhal on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120685659/ 9 "Puran Chand Aggarwal v. Lekh Raj", 210 (2014) DLT 131 where the court held as follows : "26. As far as business is concerned, it is not necessary that the landlord must show some evidence that he has experience of said business. That is not the requirement of law in order to file the eviction petition on the grounds of bonafide requirement." , MANU/SC/1719/2009MANU/SC/1719/2009: (2010) 1 SCC 164, it was observed that a person can start a new business even if he has no experience in the new business. Many people start new businesses even if they do not have experience in the new business and sometimes they are successful in the new business also. Infact, it is not even necessary for the landlord to disclose the specific business that she wants to set up and such non- disclosure would not take away her bonafide need to carry out a business, as held in "Balwant Singh Chowdhary & Anr. vs. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd.", 2004 (1) RCR 487 and "Gurcharan Lal Kumar vs. Srimati Satyawati & Ors.", MANU/DE/1078/2013: 2013 (2) RCR (Rent) 120. Even though the petitioner has categorically disclosed the precise nature of her business, nobody can ever bind her to start the exact same business in the premises after it has been vacated. A mere assertion on the part of the tenant would not be sufficient to rebut the strong presumption in the RC ARC No. 23/2023 Inderjeet Kaur Vs. Anil Kumar Singhal Page no. 19 of 25 landlord's favor that her requirement of occupation of the premises is real and genuine (see "Viran Wali Vs. Kuldeep Rai Kochhar", 174 (2010) Delhi Law Times 328). 28. 30. He has also stated that the present petition is hit by bar contained in Section 14(6) DRCA as the petitioner did not wait for the mandatory period of 5 years from the date of the death of her husband which occurred on 12.10.2022. As far as his reliance on case titled "Beena Vs. Charan Dass" (S. No. 14 supra) is concerned where it was held that consent order passed in legal proceedings cannot confer ownership rights upon party having no legal instrument, this is not a case where title has been conferred upon the petitioner/her husband by a consent order.
